messages:
sam: Heads up — CI started failing in the gcc13/bookworm matrix when building the paged + fused attention kernels. Linker error looks like a classic non-PIC object being turned into a shared lib.

CI-bot: build: failed (eng-runtime/gcc13-bookworm) — see logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/8452

sam: log excerpt:
```
/usr/bin/ld: build/_deps/flashkernels/flash_kernels.o: relocation R_X86_64_32S against `.rodata' can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

priya: Ugh. That looks like nvcc not propagating -fPIC to the device host objects. Are we passing `-Xcompiler -fPIC` in the cuda compile flags? Also check whether any static archives are being linked into a .so.

jules: I hit this before — two things to check quickly: the docker base image (glibc vs musl) and the nvcc args. On older images we used `set(CUDA_NVCC_FLAGS "${CUDA_NVCC_FLAGS} -Xcompiler=-fPIC")` in CMake. If someone changed packaging to build a static .a and then link into a shared target, ld will complain.

alex: FWIW there's also a perf regression tied to a recent patch that changed kernel selection heuristics. The selector now prefers fused attention for seq_len=128 in some batched profiles — but fused kernel there regresses memory traffic and thrashes the KV cache, raising p95 token latency ~12% on our chat-200 workload. Might be unrelated but landed close in time. Profiling attached.

priya: Good catch. We should split work: infra/CI fix for the -fPIC/linker problem, and a separate rollback or tweak for the kernel selector if perf confirms. Can someone paste the CMakeLists snippet?

jules: Quick patch I tested locally (works with gcc13 image):
```cmake
# force PIC for all CUDA host objects
if(CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER)
  set(CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS} -Xcompiler=-fPIC")
endif()
```
Also make sure any `add_library(foo STATIC ...)` that later becomes part of a shared target is not built without PIC.

sam: @priya @jules — thanks. Can we also check the builder image? The failing jobs are only on `redwood/build:bookworm-gcc13-cuda12` not on `ubuntu20-gcc12`. If it's purely toolchain, we should pin the CI matrix to gcc12 until fixed.

nikhil: Quick repro script I used (inside docker image):
```bash
# reproduce in container
docker run -it redwood/build:bookworm-gcc13-cuda12 bash -lc '
  git checkout ci-repro && mkdir build && cd build && cmake .. && make -j8'
```
This reproduces the linker error for me. Changing `CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS` above fixes it.

alex: On the perf side, I ran a tiny eval: fused kernel picks for seq=128 -> p95 token latency +11.6% (compared to baseline flash-paged). KV cache miss rate goes from 2.3% -> 6.8% on the sampling trace (same prompts). So selector needs a safety check for batch shape distribution and a qps-latency guard.

priya: Action items: 1) jules open PR to add `-Xcompiler=-fPIC` and add a CI job that builds the shared libs. 2) eng-infra to pin/remove gcc13 in the release matrix until we confirm. 3) alex to file an eval issue with perf numbers and a reproducer for selector behavior. 4) sam to coordinate roll-forward/rollback plan.

sam: I'll file the infra ticket and pin the matrix for now. @jules please include a test that builds both static and shared variants in CI.

jules: Will do, drafting PR now. Also adding a short note in the kernel packaging docs about PIC and nvcc pitfalls.

CI-bot: issue opened: #4527 (eng-runtime: flash-kernel PIC + CI matrix pin)

nikhil: tiny suggestion: also run `readelf -Ws` on the object files in CI job to fail early if any symbol is non-PIC. We can grep for `R_X86_64_32` in linker map.

sam: cool. thanks everyone. let's keep this thread for status updates. :thumbsup:
